title: Counting words
description:
Fill in three functions for a word-counting tool. The words arrive already split, as a list of strings.

```lua-norun
count_words(words)      -- a table: word -> how many times it appears
most_common(counts)     -- the word with the highest count and that count (two results);
                        -- ties go to the word that comes first alphabetically; nil for an empty table
unique_sorted(words)    -- a list of the different words, sorted alphabetically
```

```lua-norun
local counts = count_words({ "b", "a", "b" })   --> { b = 2, a = 1 }
most_common(counts)                             --> "b", 2
unique_sorted({ "b", "a", "b" })                --> { "a", "b" }
```

solution.solution.lua:
function count_words(words)
    local counts = {}
    for _, w in ipairs(words) do
        counts[w] = (counts[w] or 0) + 1
    end
    return counts
end

function most_common(counts)
    local best_word, best_count = nil, 0
    for word, count in pairs(counts) do
        if count > best_count or (count == best_count and word < best_word) then
            best_word, best_count = word, count
        end
    end
    if best_word == nil then return nil end
    return best_word, best_count
end

function unique_sorted(words)
    local seen, out = {}, {}
    for _, w in ipairs(words) do
        if not seen[w] then
            seen[w] = true
            out[#out + 1] = w
        end
    end
    table.sort(out)
    return out
end

hints: `(counts[w] or 0) + 1` starts a missing word at 0.
`pairs` visits the words in no particular order, so a tie needs its own test: `count == best_count and word < best_word`.
A table of `seen[w] = true` tells you whether a word is already in the list.
Sorting comes properly in the next lesson; for now, `table.sort(list)` sorts a list of strings alphabetically, in place: after `local t = { "b", "c", "a" }; table.sort(t)`, t is `{ "a", "b", "c" }`.
unitTests:
local words = { "the", "cat", "and", "the", "hat", "and", "the" }

test("counting", function()
    local counts = count_words(words)
    check_eq(counts, { the = 3, cat = 1, ["and"] = 2, hat = 1 })
    check_eq(count_words({}), {})
end)

test("the most common word", function()
    local word, count = most_common(count_words(words))
    check_eq(word, "the")
    check_eq(count, 3)
end)

test("ties go to the alphabetically first word", function()
    local word, count = most_common({ pear = 2, apple = 2, fig = 1 })
    check_eq(word, "apple")
    check_eq(count, 2)
    check_eq(most_common({}), nil)
end)

test("unique words, sorted", function()
    check_eq(unique_sorted(words), { "and", "cat", "hat", "the" })
    check_eq(unique_sorted({ "z" }), { "z" })
    check_eq(unique_sorted({}), {})
end)
